column1: # keyed by the file's lowercase filename stem (`scott::looks_like_scott` + the
# picker's `scott_title`). The internal adventure number in a `.dat` trailer is
# NOT a reliable key: Brian Howarth's "Mysterious Adventures" reuse numbers 1-11
# and would collide with Scott Adams's own 1-14, and licensed/Questprobe titles
# have no distinguishing number at all. The filename is the disambiguator, and
# the same game shipped under several filenames (e.g. the graphics `.blb` blorb
# repackaging of the Mysterious Adventures) gets one row per filename.
# Trailing columns are optional; leave an inner column empty (two tabs) to skip
# it while still supplying a later one (e.g. author with no TUID). Author and
# description are only used for games with no IFDB record to fetch them from; a
# real IFDB fetch always outranks these. Blank lines and lines starting with '#'
# are ignored. Keys are matched case-insensitively (the lookup lowercases the
# stem), so store them lowercase here.
# A WRONG entry mislabels a game; a MISSING one just falls back to the filename.
# The optional third column is the IFDB game id (https://ifdb.org/viewgame?id=<TUID>)
# used to fetch metadata/cover, because a Scott `.dat` has no embedded IFID and
# its computed IFID never resolves on IFDB. TUIDs were page-verified on IFDB
# (title + author confirmed) on 2026-07-17. Rows with no TUID have no IFDB entry:
# the Adventureland Sampler, and the eight miscellaneous homebrew games at the
# bottom (title/author taken from their readme and each game's own title screen).
# Provenance: filename->title mappings from the ScottFree collection readmes ---
# b_waxworks), the blorb repackaging ReadBlorb.txt (golden_baton .. waxworks),
# and the miscellaneous "Scott Adams Format" otheradv readme.txt (bond .. secret,
# identities verified against each `.dat`'s embedded title/room text).
# Brian Howarth's Mysterious Adventures (1981-1983) --- text-only `.dat` version
# Mysterious Adventures --- graphics `.blb` blorb repackaging (same games)
# Miscellaneous homebrew "Scott Adams Format" games (no IFDB entry): title, an
# empty TUID column, author, and a one-line description from the otheradv
# readme. Identities verified against each `.dat`'s embedded title/room text.

column5: Collect four lost treasures in a mine.
A Scott-format spy adventure featuring the villain Dr. Yes; the author is unknown, though Bruce Hansen has been suggested.
As an ambitious burglar, steal five valuable treasures from a poorly-secured museum without tripping an alarm or waking the sleeping guard.
A Star Trek-inspired adventure: as a Romulan spy testing a new cloaking device, infiltrate and destroy a Federation base, with cameos by Captain Kirk and Harlan Ellison.
Stop the villainous Dr. Yes from using his weather machine to take over the world, at any cost.
Little is known about this adventure; it may be based on the science-fantasy RPG published by TSR.
The title screen marks this as number ten in a series, though which series is meant is unknown.
Part I of a series; whether any further parts exist is unknown.
